name: Distance-preserving five-legged spider
summary: A phase-free five-legged Z-spider is fault-equivalent to a 5-cycle of three-legged Z-spiders.
description:
A five-legged Z-spider can be replaced by a pentagon of five three-legged Z-spiders, one for each leg, without changing the distance of any code or circuit containing it (a distance-preserving, equivalently fault-equivalent, rewrite).

Fault equivalence is with respect to *edge-flip noise*: every edge of the diagram can suffer a Pauli $X$, $Y$ or $Z$ flip of weight 1. The pentagon is a detecting region for $X$-flips, so only even numbers of internal $X$-flips are undetectable, and these, as well as all $Z$-flips, can be pushed to the outer legs without increasing their weight. Together with [the four-legged version](../fe-four-legged-spider/) and the general decompositions of [even](../fe-even-spider-decomposition/) and [odd](../fe-odd-spider-decomposition/) spiders, this reduces any spider to spiders of degree at most three.
